title: Catharinus hard to square with Trent sess. 6 cap. 9; commonly rejected after the Council
source_text: XVI. Verum haec Ambrosii Catharini sententia difficulter videtur conciliari posse cum Tridentinae Synodi decreto, quod habetur Sess. 6. cap. 9. sub finem. Ubi asseritur quod Nullus scire valeat certitudine fidei, cui non potest subesse falsum, se gratiam Dei esse consecutum. Ideoque post Concilium Tridentinum, sententia haec, tanquam erronea, communiter in Schola Romana rejecta est: licet Catharinus ille, qui Concilii istius pars fuit, eam non tantum semper retinuerit, sed publice quoque defenderit, tanquam minime damnatam in Concilio Tridentino, cujus verba pretendit, ex mente eorum qui decretum condiderunt, dogma illud suum non ferire.
pass_a_gloss: But this opinion of Ambrosius Catharinus seems difficult to reconcile with the decree of the Tridentine Synod, which is found in Session 6, chapter 9, toward the end. Where it is asserted that No one can know with the certainty of faith, to which falsehood cannot be subject, that he has obtained the grace of God. And therefore after the Council of Trent this opinion, as erroneous, has been commonly rejected in the Roman School: although that Catharinus, who was part of that Council, not only always retained it, but also publicly defended it as by no means condemned in the Council of Trent, whose words he pretends, from the mind of those who framed the decree, not to strike that dogma of his.
pass_b_english: Trent session 6 chapter 9 denies faith-certainty that one has obtained grace.
After Trent Catharinus’s view is commonly rejected, though he still claimed the Council did not condemn him.
